children: Copper prices headed towards a record high on Monday, as the prospect of shortages outside the U.S. spurred buying, while the softer dollar reinforced positive sentiment.
Traders said a U.S. holiday meant volumes were likely to be muted, but added that focus was firmly on copper and zinc.
on the London Metal Exchange was up 0.1% at $14,430 a metric ton at 0931 GMT, the highest since the all-time peak of $14,527.50 hit in January.

Traders and producers have been shipping copper to the U.S. since President Donald Trump mooted import tariffs in February last year. Comex copper stocks (HG-STX-COMEX) stood at a record high of 766,795 short tons, or 695,624 metric tons.
Elevated premiums or backwardations for nearby

contracts against longer-dated forwards have attracted some copper back to the LME. But cancelled warrants or metal earmarked for delivery at 51% indicate more than 121,000 tons of copper are likely to leave the LME system over the coming days and weeks. (0#MCUSTX-LOC).
The premium for the cash over the three-month forward (CMCU0-3) climbed above $430 a ton in the middle of August, the highest since 2021. It closed around $74 on Friday.

Another sign of tight supplies outside the U.S. is stocks in warehouses monitored by the Shanghai Futures Exchange (CU-STX-SGH) at 63,000 tons, down 85% since the middle of March and at their lowest since January 2024.
Copper prices on ShFE are also in backwardation (0#SCF:) suggesting the industry in top consumer China is also worried about supplies.
, supported by tight supplies and low LME stocks (MZNSTX-TOTAL) was up 0.8% at $3,976 a ton, close to the $3,990 a ton hit at the start of the month, the highest since May 2022.
A softer U.S. currency, which makes dollar-priced metals cheaper for holders of other currencies, supported base metals overall.
